In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA content is kept at the n to 2n level in the early stage of erythropoieses, but in later stage, polychromatic erythroblasts and reticulocytes have the DNA level of 4n or more.
in normal erythroblastic development the DNA level is kept at 1 to 2 n until late stages of the erythroblasts, but in anemia, the DNA level is decreased to n or 0 in the early stages.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the erythroblasts in anemic animals are in the state of DNA synthesis and that they are in the stage of DNA synthesis and denucleation in the recovery stage of the animals receiving a mass red transfusion.

the Feulgen reaction of the erythroblast nuclei in the bone marrow is kept at a level of n to 2n until the basophilic normoblast stage, and that in later stages, the DNA level of the nucleus is decreased in the polychromatic normoblasts and the orthochromic normoblasts.

the Feulgen reaction in the nucleus of erythroblasts of normal rabbit bone marrow is kept in the range of 0.2 to 0.5 optical density units, and that the DNA level of these nuclei is kept at 0 to 2 n levels from the proerythoblast to the late basophilic erythroblast.
